title: Etale/pro-etale comparison reflects local integer torsion
statement: For any scheme X, commutative ring A, and etale sheaf F of A-modules, if the underlying abelian sheaf of its pro-etale inverse image is locally torsion, then F is a torsion module sheaf. There is no uniform annihilator assumption.

source.place: Opening paragraph: descend local torsion; Stacks 03SA, 0993, 0GLZ

proof.text: Represent a pro-etale geometric stalk germ on a pointed weakly etale neighbourhood. Apply local torsion to a representing section. A member of its covering lifts the algebraically closed geometric point: base change the cover, use joint surjectivity, and split the resulting nonempty weakly etale scheme over the algebraically closed field. Restriction to that pointed member preserves the germ and kills the section by a positive integer. Hence the pro-etale stalk is a torsion group.

The canonical comparison-stalk isomorphism identifies this stalk with the etale module stalk of F. Forgetting module scalars commutes with its filtered colimit. The conservative family of algebraically closed etale points reflects local torsion on the underlying abelian sheaf, which is equivalent to IsTorsionModuleSheaf.

theorem comparisonUpperStar_reflects_local_torsion (X : Scheme.{u})
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))
    (hF : ((sheafCompose (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
      (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj
        ((comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).obj F)).IsTorsion) :
    Scheme.IsTorsionModuleSheaf F
